title: Examples that teach the format
goal: Use labelled demonstrations to obtain consistent complaint summaries.
explanation: Three demonstrations make this a few-shot exercise, not a one-shot exercise. A model can imitate their punctuation while still misunderstanding a complaint. Hold back one email until you have written the format rules, then test an ambiguous case as well as the easy one.
sampleInput:
Email 1: My parcel was due Monday. It is Wednesday and nothing arrived. → Summary: Delivery — parcel two days late.
Email 2: The receipt shows $18 but my card was charged $23. → Summary: Billing — charged $5 above receipt.
Email 3: The lid cracked on first use. → Summary: Product — lid cracked on first use.
Held-out email: I paid for two notebooks; the parcel contained one.
prompt:
Learn the summary format from the three labelled examples. Summarize only the held-out email as “Summary: Category — one factual issue.” Use Delivery, Billing, Product or Needs review. Do not invent a cause, remedy or refund.
[Paste examples and held-out email.]
workedExample: Acceptable held-out result: Summary: Delivery — one of two paid notebooks missing. “Billing — customer charged twice” is not supported: the complaint concerns a missing item, not two payments.

steps.title: Prepare the demonstrations
steps.text: Copy the first three input/output pairs and name the allowed categories.

steps.title: Hold one case back
steps.text: Keep the notebook email out of the demonstrations; write your own expected summary before querying.

steps.title: Run the few-shot prompt
steps.text: Compare its output with your reference on category, issue, prefix and invented facts.

steps.title: Try ambiguity
steps.text: Replace the held-out email with “It happened again.” A safe result asks for review rather than inventing a specific issue.

steps.title: Refine one example
steps.text: If the notebook case fails, add a missing-item example and test a new held-out email, not the same one only.

checks: The held-out summary captures one missing notebook without claiming a duplicate payment.
The ambiguous email receives Needs review or a clarification, not invented details.
The exact prefix, category separator and one-issue rule remain consistent across three new tests.
commonMistakes: Evaluating only on examples already shown to the model.
Calling formatting consistency evidence of factual accuracy.
offline: Classify the four emails on paper, then ask a partner to infer your formatting rule from the first three.
reflection: What changed when you improved the examples: the category decision, the formatting, or both?

evidence.title: Keep the build
evidence.detail: Save your original input, exact prompt and resulting artifact. The held-out summary captures one missing notebook without claiming a duplicate payment.

evidence.title: Show what you tested
evidence.detail: Record a pass/fail result and evidence for every check below. The ambiguous email receives Needs review or a clarification, not invented details.

evidence.title: Explain a limitation
evidence.detail: Write what changed after one deliberate revision and name a remaining failure mode. Evaluating only on examples already shown to the model.
